scope: Selected-section review of language, verification and tooling feature families, covering reference-manual chapters 3–15. Not an exhaustive AST-constructor audit or a claim of complete implementation.

features.assessment: Requires clauses and imported NatSpec preconditions already generate checked obligations.
features.next: Preserve argument binding and definedness; add source-associated diagnostics.

features.assessment: Ensures, result values and contract invariants are already supported for admitted source shapes.
features.next: Associate failed obligations with their source specifications.

features.assessment: Entry snapshots cover storage and ledger; there is no general labeled-state expression surface.
features.next: Add typed labeled snapshots and reusable two-state predicates if needed.

features.assessment: Both forall and exists are supported over primitive domains, including checked Presburger quantifier alternation and array-property fragments. General specification collection domains remain incomplete. The source compiler rejects snapshot/return binder capture and preserves primitive-binder shadowing of reference paths.
features.next: Extend typed specification domains and checked quantifier automation.

features.assessment: Assignable syntax already names roots, fields, indices and wildcard descendants; general modular frame application remains limited. Dafny write restrictions and local final-state framing differ.
features.next: Carry precise assigns information into effectful contract application.

features.assessment: Supported invariant loop rules have soundness proofs; present does not cover every memory or callback body.
features.next: Extend explicitly unsupported loop-body shapes.

features.assessment: Computed loop anonymisation tracks storage roots. Aliases, memory and finer locations remain conservative.
features.next: Introduce typed finer location sets, alias-aware effects and memory frames.

features.assessment: Unsigned scalar variants and typed NatSpec tuple measures are supported. Ordinary diamond loops with an admitted frame, no break flag and no quantified invariant clauses generate lexicographic VCs that require all components to be defined and a strict decrease after every successful body turn. Box and callback proofs retain partial-correctness erasure. Ordinary diamonds still accept exhaustion; separate statement-indexed SourceCertificate values certify successful runs of the exact declared tuple. Signed/general source metrics and total recursive termination remain open.
features.next: Broaden admitted frames, invariant clauses and metric sorts; add checked first-iteration reasoning for do-while; connect automatic VCs to strict successful-termination certificates and establish callback and recursive total termination.

features.assessment: UseContract already applies callee contracts. Automatic summaries cover restricted value computations and do not provide arbitrary precise effectful summaries.
features.next: Add effectful summaries with checked frames and explicit read dependencies.

features.assessment: Recursive contracts, including callbacks, are proved by induction over bounded unrolling with accepted exhaustion. This is not Dafny total-termination parity.
features.next: Add a separately stated total-correctness result with genuine decreases.

features.assessment: Lean supplies ghost proof variables; a source-level ghost declaration, update and erasure discipline is absent.
features.next: If adding source ghost state, prove noninterference with runtime state.

features.assessment: Lean definitions and theorems provide reusable lemmas; the source specification language has no general named predicate or lemma-call layer.
features.next: Expose checked reusable specification predicates without new trusted axioms.

features.assessment: Lean tactic blocks and checked calculus chains provide proof authoring facilities; Dafny source syntax is not implemented.
features.next: Only add source-associated proof syntax for a concrete authoring need.

features.assessment: Lean abstraction and explicit rewriting cover host proof control; there is no Dafny reveal statement in Solidity specs.
features.next: Use explicit checked rewrite lemmas; optional source proof surface remains separate.

features.assessment: Solidity assert panics at runtime whereas Dafny assert is erased. Proof assumptions must not be presented as proved runtime behavior.
features.next: Keep ghost assertions distinct and report unchecked assumptions explicitly.

features.assessment: Explicitly typed finite equality-membership and literal-domain filtered membership are admitted in source specifications. Filter keys must denote values and guards use a typed inner scope; the existing equality-membership semantics for halting terms is unchanged. First-class collections, cardinality, sequences, multisets and mathematical maps remain absent from the source interface.
features.next: Add reusable collection models and operations with explicit definedness and typed denotation; preserve the distinction from finite equality-membership.

features.assessment: Source specifications support finite literal-domain identity filters with a genuine typed guard binder. The key stays in the outer scope and must denote a value; every operand is checked even for an empty domain. Domains are primitive literals, guard equality retains existing KeY semantics, constants are handled conservatively and the new form is explicitly unsupported in loop annotations. General images, multiple binders and first-class collection values remain open.
features.next: Extend domain and image fragments with typed denotation and explicit definedness; implement first-class collections and reusable source predicates separately.

features.assessment: Solidity bounded signed/unsigned arithmetic and mathematical KeY int exist. Their semantics deliberately differ from Dafny unbounded numeric defaults.
features.next: Preserve widths, checked overflow and division failures when extending admitted arithmetic.

features.assessment: Dafny floating-point, real and ordinal runtime types are not Solidity runtime types. Host mathematical models are separate.
features.next: No runtime implementation required for Solidity parity.

features.assessment: Dependent contexts and bounded values encode invariants; Solidity value types follow Solidity semantics rather than Dafny subset/newtype rules.
features.next: Use host refinements for proof invariants; source refinements need their own checked interface.

features.assessment: Lean inductive families already model syntax and proof data. Solidity enum and struct behavior remains separate.
features.next: No new runtime syntax required; optional ghost model types can remain host Lean.

features.assessment: Typed storage, memory and aliases are implemented with explicit remaining source and recursive-type gaps. Fresh/allocated specification expressions are not generally exposed.
features.next: Add typed allocation observations and complete reference-bearing source shapes.

features.assessment: Lean provides higher-order models. Solidity function values are separately inventoried; Dafny generic/lambda runtime semantics do not transfer directly.
features.next: Separate higher-order ghost models from Solidity function-value execution.

features.assessment: Contract inheritance, overrides and libraries already have a Solidity feature inventory; Dafny classes/traits are analogues, not equivalent semantics.
features.next: Follow solc declaration identity, initialization and dispatch requirements.

features.assessment: Lean modules organize proofs; Solidity imports are separately modeled. Dafny abstract/export/refinement modules have no direct Solidity counterpart.
features.next: Express contract refinement as explicit correctness theorems when required.

features.assessment: Solidity has no Dafny yield/iterator construct. Lean can represent coinductive or trace models without changing Solidity runtime syntax.
features.next: Add trace abstractions only for a concrete verification claim.

features.assessment: Assignments, calls, branches, loops and break/continue already exist; admitted shapes and remaining gaps are in the Solidity inventory. Tuple annotations survive loop-local scope, renaming, nested loops and break/continue/return lowering. Declaration-ID renaming preserves lexical shadowing, specification bindings, named call labels and counterexample source positions. Dafny match/binding guards are separate constructs.
features.next: Complete admitted Solidity shapes rather than introducing unrelated Dafny syntax.

features.assessment: Typed havoc and external response/callback abstractions exist. Such-that assignments and arbitrary ghost nondeterminism lack a general source surface.
features.next: Retain explicit typed models and abstraction premises.

features.assessment: Bounded search, heartbeat limits, chunked proofs and runner timeouts exist; editor resource and cancellation behavior needs tests.
features.next: Expose stable per-obligation timing and reliable cancellation.

features.assessment: Lean induction and checked replay provide host proof automation. Dafny SMT trigger syntax is not implemented or necessary for existing kernel proofs.
features.next: Prefer checked reusable lemmas and bounded replay to unchecked solver claims.

features.assessment: The opt-in source pipeline exposes a kernel-certified refutation of the exact original Fml.Valid obligation with the same typed model prestate. Primitive argument values, transaction, initial storage, ledger and balance are retained; exact declaration IDs and parameter indices add source names. The editor validates the transport and suppresses stale or unsolicited results. Positioned model-state sequences, general collection expansion, constructor reachability, replay, complete post-states and general callback or recursive witnesses remain open.
features.next: Extend certified source witnesses to additional semantic readings and positioned intermediate model states.

features.assessment: Axiom checks remain. Entry-condition auditing now retains kernel-checked certificates of impossibility or possibility tied to the original scoped obligation; bounded failure is unknown. CLI and editor auditing are opt-in and impossible/unknown checks cannot pass strict suites. Constructor reachability and general dead-code analysis remain open.
features.next: Extend assurance to constructor reachability and unreachable branches; entry possibility alone does not establish a successful execution.

features.assessment: Source verification runners and checked fixtures exist. General Dafny-style coverage-guided test generation is not implemented.
features.next: Export certified counterexamples as reproducible regression inputs.

features.assessment: Lake artifacts, source runners and JSON reports exist. A stable editor/CLI protocol is a separate integration contract.
features.next: Preserve report status, source identity and configuration semantics across clients.

features.assessment: The Solidity Lean extension provides a persistent LSP for exact unsaved snapshots, compiler-backed completion/navigation/signatures/rename, diagnostics, hover, gutters, Testing and automatic verification. Lean proof workers retain import environments; exact reports are cached with source/options/dependency identities. Opt-in entry audits and certified model prestates remain supported. Formatting, project services, positioned execution traces and full Dafny parity remain open.
features.next: Extend receiver-aware completion, project ownership/includes, formatting, code actions and positioned traces; within-file proof scheduling remains serial.

features.assessment: Lean metaprogramming and optional Bridge provide extension points. Dafny compiler backends for other languages are not Solidity requirements.
features.next: Keep the core dependency-free; place optional adapters in separate packages.
